newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-Paris/Asia cargo rates may rise post surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Paris/Asia cargo rates may rise post surcharge.

text.p: Some air cargo rates to Asia from Paris are set to rise and take advantage of the removal of the fuel surcharge after an otherwise static period, a Reuters survey showed.
In the past month average air cargo rates ex-Paris to the Far East, with one or two exceptions, have largely held stable .
However, market pacesetter, Air France, says it has earmarked increases on two key routes in the sector following the recent withdrawal of the fuel surcharge.
"We're planning increases of 50 centimes/kilo on ex-France routes to Hong Kong and Japan, probably from mid-May," an Air France Cargo official told Reuters.
This will work out at a six percent increase to Hong Kong and around 3.5 percent to Japan, the official said.
"Hong Kong is our best-performing destination at present and we raised our rates on the route by about 30 centimes/kilo on March 1.
Cathay Pacific, the other maindeck carrier on the Paris-HKG route, increased its ex-France rates by four to five percent from March 17.

"As far as Japan is concerned, our rates are now a little below those of Japan Airlines since we withdrew the fuel surcharge so the mid-May increase will more or less bring these into line with theirs," the Air France Cargo official added.
JAL, with whom Air France operates joint freighter services between Paris and Tokyo, did not apply the surcharge and last increased its ex-Paris rates by three to four percent in January 1997.
Air France Cargo was also considering rates increases elsewhere in the Far East, notably Singapore, Korea and Thailand but a firm decision had yet to be taken, the official added.
Korean Airlines, which had also withdrawn the fuel surcharge, applied a general increase in its ex-France rates from April 1, averaging out at five percent.
A Paris-based KAL cargo official said the biggest increases centred on Japan and several destinations in the Pacific Rim, for example, Honolulu, Guam and Saipan.
Meanwhile, Singapore Airlines, said it had increased its rates from Paris rates by an average of five percent to "selected destinations" in the Far East but excluding Singapore itself.
While we have withdrawn the fuel surcharge, it's unlikely we'll be increasing rates from Paris to Singapore before October," said David Lim, SIA's London-based regional cargo manager, Europe.
The joint SIA/Air France B747-200F service between Paris and Singapore was upgraded from three to five weekly frequencies, effective last week.
"The extra frequencies are living up to our expectations in load factor terms," Lim added.
From June 1 1997, SIA plans to replace its two 747-200Fs plying the route with 400F "Mega Arks" which offer ten to 20 tonnes extra capacity per flight as a result of an extra main deck position.
Air France is expected to announce an upgrade in its services from Paris to China during President Jacques Chirac's visit to the People's Republic next month.
Industry sources said the airline was considering the launch of a three times weekly passenger service to Shanghai using Airbus 340s, providing significant belly-capacity for freight.
However, an Air France official could not confirm these reports.
The French carrier currently operates a weekly Boeing 747-200F stopover at Shanghai in association with China Eastern Airlines.

In an interview earlier this year, in French freight transport magazine, Transports Actualites, Air France Cargo chief, Francois Bachelet, said the airline was looking to forge alliances in Asia, singling out China for particular mention.
Air France also operates a four weekly frequencies on its passenger service between Paris and Beijing operated by Boeing 747-400 combis.
Malaysian Air System said it will be taking a weekly block booking on Air France's freighter service between Paris/Charles de Gaulle (CDG) and Kuala Lumpur.
"From June 1, we will have a 30-tonne allocation on one of Air France' Boeing 747-200F two weekly flights on the route," a Paris-based MAS cargo official told Reuters.

MAS' cargo capacity from Charles de Gaulle airport was reduced significantly last month when the Malaysian carrier withdrew Boeing 747 combis from its three-times weekly passenger Paris-Kuala Lumpur service replacing them with 747 PAX aircraft.

To compensate partially for the withdrawal of the combis on the CDG-Kuala Lumpur route, MAS' Paris cargo station had increased its allocation of offline freighter and maindeck capacity offered jointly by the Malaysian carrier and KLM from Schiphol, the official said.

"With the block booking on the Air France freighter and our offline options from Amsterdam, our Paris station will more or less have the same level of capacity as its disposal before the combis were withdrawn."
Thai Airways has put extra capacity on its Paris-Bangkok route in introducing an additional Boeing 747 freighter frequency, effective end-March.
Thai already operated a twice-weekly Paris-Bangkok 747F service in conjunction with Air France but the new frequency is independent of the French carrier.
Thai, which also transports freight in the bellyhold of a daily passenger service on the route, increased ex-Paris rates by around five percent from March 1.

Commenting on the French air cargo market as a whole, Klaus Pfab, the president of France's air freight forwarders association, told Reuters last week: "So far, 1997 has been below our expectations in volume terms and this is reflected in the moderate level rate increases implemented by several airlines in March and during the current month."

Further increases are unlikely before the autumn and Pfab said that one positive factor from the fuel surcharges was that airlines seemed to have finally understood the importance of prior notice on rates increases.

Although Paris rates have been fairly stable, their yield is still below other European centres meaning carriers would prefer to operate tyhere leaving French shippers and agents short of capacity, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
